title: Local constancy and base change of projective fibre Hilbert polynomials
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $n\geq0$, and let $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that $Z\to T$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented, meaning locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], quasi-compact and quasi-separated. For $t\in T$, let $P_t\in\mathbf Q[x]$ be the unique polynomial eventually equal to the dimensions of the homogeneous pieces of the homogeneous coordinate ring of $Z_{\overline{\kappa(t)}}$ for its induced projective embedding. This polynomial exists, is numerical, has degree at most $n$ when nonzero, and equals $d\mapsto\chi(Z_{\overline{\kappa(t)}},\mathcal O_Z(d))$, where $\chi$ denotes the alternating sum of the dimensions of coherent cohomology. The map $t\mapsto P_t$ is locally constant. For every morphism $h:T'\to T$ and every $t'\in T'$, the polynomial of $(Z\times_TT')_{\overline{\kappa(t')}}$ is $P_{h(t')}$. This includes $Z=\varnothing$, whose polynomial is zero; a projective scheme over a field has zero Hilbert polynomial if and only if it is empty.

source.place: Tag 0B9T (lemma-chi-locally-constant-geometric), applied to twists; varieties.tex Tags 08AC (lemma-hilbert-polynomial) and 08AE (lemma-hilbert-polynomial-H0). Constancy of the polynomial follows from n+1 Euler characteristics; the field-polynomial comparison is Serre vanishing.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-projective-twist-base-change-data] to obtain properness of $f:Z\to T$ and finitely presented base-flat twists $\mathcal F_d$, with their base-change identifications. For every $d\in\mathbf Z$, [lem-sfb-proper-flat-sheaf-euler-local-constancy] therefore gives a locally constant function $E_d(t)=\chi(Z_{\kappa(t)},\mathcal O(d))$. Its base-change clause gives $E_d(t)=\chi(Z_K,\mathcal O_{Z_K}(d))$ for every field-valued point $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ with image $t$, including geometric points and composites from any other base.

For each such field point, [lem-sfb-projective-field-coordinate-euler-polynomial] gives the unique numerical polynomial $Q_{Z_K}$, its homogeneous coordinate presentation $A$, and eventual equality with $\dim_K A_d$. Apply [lem-sfb-graded-coordinate-polynomial-degree-emptiness] to this presentation: $\deg Q_{Z_K}\leq n$ when nonzero, and $Q_{Z_K}=0$ exactly when $Z_K=\varnothing$. Put $P_t=Q_{Z_{\overline{\kappa(t)}}}$. Step 1 gives $P_t(d)=E_d(t)$ for every integer $d$. This proves all the asserted fibre-polynomial, numerical, degree and zero-polynomial clauses; the two cited results also apply directly to every projective scheme embedded over any field.

Fix $t\in T$. For each $d=0,\ldots,n$ choose an open neighbourhood $U_d$ of $t$ on which $E_d$ is constant, using step 1. On $U=\bigcap_{d=0}^nU_d$, the polynomial $P_u-P_t$ has degree at most $n$ and the $n+1$ distinct roots $0,\ldots,n$; the polynomial root bound forces it to be zero. Thus $u\mapsto P_u$ is constant on $U$. Zero polynomials and $n=0$ are included. No uniform Serre-vanishing bound on the family is used.

proof.text: For $h:T'\to T$, $t'\in T'$ and $K'=\overline{\kappa(t')}$, the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $(Z\times_TT')_{K'}$ with the pullback of $Z$ at the composite $\operatorname{Spec}K'\to T'\to T$. Step 1 identifies its twists and gives Euler values $E_d(h(t'))$; step 2 constructs its coordinate polynomial, which consequently agrees with $P_{h(t')}$ at every integer $d$. Their difference has infinitely many roots, so they are equal. This proves arbitrary base change without comparing chosen algebraic closures.

lean.statement: theorem flat_projective_hilbert_polynomial_locality {T Z : Scheme.{u}} (n : ℕ) (i : Z ⟶ RelativeProjectiveSpace.scheme T n) [IsClosedImmersion i] [Flat (i ≫ RelativeProjectiveSpace.π T n)] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (i ≫ RelativeProjectiveSpace.π T n)] [QuasiCompact (i ≫ RelativeProjectiveSpace.π T n)] [QuasiSeparated (i ≫ RelativeProjectiveSpace.π T n)] : ∃ P : T → Polynomial ℚ, IsLocallyConstant P ∧ ∃ e : RelativeProjectiveSpace.scheme T n ≅ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1)); T), e.hom ≫ (ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1)); T) ↘ T) = RelativeProjectiveSpace.π T n ∧ (∀ t : T, (∀ Q : Polynomial ℚ, IsCoordinatePolynomial (AlgebraicClosure (T.residueField t)) n (baseChangeEmbedding n (i ≫ e.hom) (geometricPoint T t)) Q ↔ Q = P t) ∧ (∀ d : ℤ, ∃ z : ℤ, (P t).eval (d : ℚ) = (z : ℚ)) ∧ ((P t) ≠ 0 → (P t).natDegree ≤ n) ∧ (∀ d : ℤ, (P t).eval (d : ℚ) = (twistEuler (AlgebraicClosure (T.residueField t)) n (baseChangeEmbedding n (i ≫ e.hom) (geometricPoint T t)) d : ℚ)) ∧ (P t = 0 ↔ IsEmpty ↥ (pullback ((i ≫ e.hom) ≫ (ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (n + 1)); T) ↘ T)) (geometricPoint T t)))) ∧ (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (h : T' ⟶ T) (t' : T') (Q : Polynomial ℚ), IsCoordinatePolynomial (AlgebraicClosure (T'.residueField t')) n (baseChangeEmbedding n (baseChangeEmbedding n (i ≫ e.hom) h) (geometricPoint T' t')) Q ↔ Q = P (h t'))
